props.gloss_en: whoever commits a transgression and is ashamed of it -- all his sins are forgiven him
Rav's proof-text: 'that you may remember and be ashamed... when I have forgiven you for all that you have done' (Ezek 16:63)
the stam's replacement source: Saul told Samuel that God no longer answered him 'by prophets or by dreams' (1 Sam 28:15) -- and did not say 'by the Urim veTumim'
Saul did not mention the Urim veTumim among the means by which God no longer answered him
[he omitted the Urim veTumim] because he had killed Nov, the city of priests
Saul was pardoned from heaven
the source that Saul was pardoned: 'tomorrow you and your sons will be with me' (1 Sam 28:19)
R' Yochanan: 'with me' means 'in my company' [among the righteous]
the Rabbis' source for the pardon: 'we will hang them up unto the Lord in the Giva of Saul, the chosen of the Lord' (2 Sam 21:6) -- a bat kol went out and said 'the chosen of the Lord'
they sought to fix parashat Balak in the recitation of the Shema
why did they not fix it? because of the burden on the congregation
(entertained) they sought to fix Balak because the Exodus is written in it -- 'God who brought them out of Egypt' (Num 23:22)
R' Yosei bar Avin: they sought to fix Balak because this verse is written in it -- 'he couched, he lay down like a lion and a lioness; who shall rouse him?' (Num 24:9)
a received tradition: any parasha that Moshe Rabbeinu divided we divide; one that Moshe Rabbeinu did not divide we do not divide
R' Yehuda bar Chaviva: parashat tzitzit was fixed because there are five things in it
the tzitzit paragraph contains the mitzva of tzitzit
the tzitzit paragraph contains the Exodus
the tzitzit paragraph contains the yoke of mitzvot
the tzitzit paragraph contains [an admonition against] the opinion of heretics
the tzitzit paragraph contains [an admonition against] thoughts of transgression
the tzitzit paragraph contains [an admonition against] thoughts of idolatry
the yoke of mitzvot is explicit: 'and you shall see it and remember all the mitzvot of the Lord' (Num 15:39)
tzitzit is explicit: 'and they shall make for themselves tzitzit' (Num 15:38)
the Exodus is explicit: 'who brought you out [of the land of Egypt]' (Num 15:41)
the baraita: 'after your hearts' -- this is heresy; and so it says, 'the fool said in his heart, there is no God' (Ps 14:1)
the baraita: 'after your eyes' -- this is thoughts of transgression, as it says, 'and Samson said to his father, take her for me, for she is right in my eyes' (Judg 14:3)
the baraita: 'you go astray' -- this is thoughts of idolatry; and so it says, 'and they went astray after the Baalim' (Judg 8:33)

objections.gloss_en: דילמא צבור שאני -- perhaps a community is different [and Ezekiel's forgiveness of the community shows nothing about an individual]
לימא פרשת רבית ופרשת משקלות דכתיב בהן יציאת מצרים -- then let them say the parasha of usury or of weights, in which the Exodus is written
ולימא האי פסוקא ותו לא -- then let them say this verse and no more
